text: sed -n '300,345p' src/ir_lower/expr/array_builtin_args.rs: N ... is deprecated` notice. USER functions do NOT get this — /// `function f(int $v) {} f(null);` is an uncaught `TypeError` — which is why this is keyed to /// the builtin registry and not to the shared argument coercion. /// /// Without it a null operand reached the builtin's own EIR lowering, which has no null case /// and PANICKED the compiler: `if ($c) { $x = "a"; } strlen($x);` — a program `php -n` 8.5.6 /// runs to `int(0)` — died with `strlen cannot lower checked operand type Void`. Adopting PHP's /// semantics for undefined variables is what made that reachable; a conditionally assigned /// variable is null on the path that skips the assignment, exactly as PHP says. /// /// The operand it replaces is left in place and still runs: it is the `warned_null` /// that raises `Warning: Undefined variable $x`, which PHP raises here too. Only the VALUE /// handed to the builtin changes.
